title: LELA: an LLM-based Entity Linking Approach with Zero-Shot Domain Adaptation
text: input. The goal of the candidate generation step is to identify the entities C m ⊆ ℰ {C_{m}\subseteq\mathcal{E}} that could potentially be relevant to m m . For this step, LELA is retriever-agnostic, and can work with any method that is capable of pre-selecting a subset of relevant entities. In practice, any generation method that requires domain-specific training would jeopardize LELA’s goal of being fine-tuning-free. Hence, we primarily consider BM25 Robertson and Sparck Jones ( 1988 ) and dense retrieval, and also experiment with prior-based dictionaries. Each candidate c ∈ C m c\in C_{m} is then given a score s ​ ( c ) ∈ ℝ s(c)\in\mathbb{R} by pointwise reranking. While any off-the-shelf reranker can be used, we opt for instructed rerankers, as the candidate entity reranking task is not typically covered during reranker training. Rerankers based on generative language models typically take as input a query q q , a document d d , and a reranking-instruction I I .
